assumptions: All graphs and digraphs are finite and simple unless the statement explicitly says otherwise.

definitions.definition: The graph whose vertices are pairwise intersection points of circles and whose edges are the circle arcs between consecutive intersection points.
No three great circles pass through one common point.
A vertex coloring with three colors in which adjacent vertices have distinct colors.

domain.description: Simple finite arrangements of great circles on the sphere and their embedded arrangement graphs.

quantifiers.domain: finite sets of great circles on the sphere with no triple concurrence
proper vertex colorings of the arrangement graph using at most three colors

statement.text: Is the arrangement graph of every finite set of great circles on the sphere with no three circles meeting at one point properly vertex 3-colorable?

title: 3-colorability of arrangements of great circles
